summary.intent: Complete trail 154, a performance effort to bring shadcn extraction with dependencies loaded back to the 141 ms / 275 MiB baseline, then publish the resulting branches as stacked PRs.
summary.outcome: A worker built two perf branches that cut shadcn wall time about 6% and peak memory about 5% but did not reach the baseline. They were pushed as draft PRs #284 and #285 (stacked), and the third planned branch was dropped after measurement.

repo: Shadcn `extract --json --no-cache` output includes a changing `durationMs` field, so output hashes differ between runs of the same binary unless that field is stripped before comparing.
`just bench` compares against origin/main using Mantine and Chakra with dependencies off. Its thresholds are 1.10 for time and 1.20 for memory.
A file's package demands all share the same `from` path, so the derived `Ord` compared a long path first on every comparison. Sorting by (specifier, name) is cheaper.

The React-augmentation search kept a full parse of every file it passed through. Files that cannot declare into React only need a re-exports scan, but any file mentioning `declare module "react"` or `namespace React` still needs a full parse.

Module-only imports can be resolved once per resolution scope, the nearest ancestor with package.json, tsconfig.json, jsconfig.json or node_modules. On shadcn this cuts 2748 demands to about 1316 resolutions. The assumption may break where a tsconfig `references` list picks a config by `include`.
Loading dependencies on shadcn costs about 70 ms and 175 MiB (164 ms / 313 MiB with, 95 ms / 139 MiB without), which is the main remaining gap to the baseline.

A persisted dependency index only makes a warm run about 4% faster (158 ms vs 164 ms for `--no-cache`). A parse cache would not help the `--no-cache` acceptance target and would touch ADRs 0003, 0008 and 0011.
Full nextest needs to run unsandboxed because the watch/pty tests need it.

code.finding: The existing assertion that a scan-only file is kept in the layer's parse map now asserts it is not kept, reflecting the lean scan change.

workflow: On a loaded machine (load average 9–15), only compare benchmark numbers measured side by side in interleaved runs, and take the median.

A cheaper estimate obtained by disabling a code path entirely, such as the 5.5 ms figure for `merged_interfaces`, can overstate the savings of caching it. Measuring the real per-call cost (about 0.25 µs) showed the cache was not worth it, and a prototype was slower because of lock contention.
Validating a new text scanner against 131,197 real `.d.ts` files from node_modules found missing `export default <import>` cases that unit tests had not caught.
Measuring a candidate (the warm-run parse cache) before prototyping it avoided building a change that could not help the target.

friction: The machine was heavily loaded (load average 9–15) throughout, so the uncontended 141 ms / 275 MiB baseline could not be reproduced and the remaining time gap could not be measured.
The two shipped branches fall short of the trail's goal, and the planned `cache-react-augmentations` branch had to be dropped after it was built and measured.
The prefilter's first run produced false negatives on `export default <import>`, which needed fixing before the branches were ready.
The assistant has not read the CI checks on the pushed PRs.
